column2: Boil the tomato, crushed garlic and thyme for 5 minutes until thick.
Preheat the oven to 230 °C; divide the dough in two and roll it out thinly on baking paper.
Spread the sauce, arrange the mozzarella and toppings and drizzle the remaining olive oil.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the edges are golden and the cheese melts.
Preheating a pizza stone or an upside-down tray makes the base crispy.
Slice and serve hot with rocket.
2 days in the fridge; reheat in a pan.
Vegetable quiche
1.5 cups flour
100 g cold butter
1 egg (for the dough)
2–3 tablespoons cold water
Filling: 3 eggs, 1 cup cream or milk
1 cup sautéed vegetables (spinach, mushrooms, leeks)
Half a teaspoon black pepper, 1 pinch nutmeg
Rub the flour, salt and diced butter with your fingertips; add the egg and water, bring together and chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C; roll out the dough into a 24 cm tart tin and prick with a fork.
Cover the dough with paper and beans and pre-bake for 12 minutes; remove the weights.
Whisk the eggs, cream, pepper and nutmeg.
Spread the vegetables and kashar on the base and pour in the liquid mixture.
Bake for 35 minutes until the centre no longer wobbles; rest for 10 minutes and slice.
Pre-baking keeps the base from staying doughy.
Lukewarm or at room temperature with a green salad.
3 days in the fridge.
Baked zucchini fritters (mücver)
3 medium zucchini (grated)
1 carrot (grated)
100 g white cheese (crumbled)
5 tablespoons flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
Sprinkle a pinch of salt on the grated zucchini, leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid well with your hands.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C and line a 20x30 cm tray with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs and add the zucchini, carrot, cheese, finely chopped herbs, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Add the flour and baking powder and mix until you get a smooth batter.
Spread the batter evenly in the tray and bake for 30–35 minutes until golden on top and a toothpick comes out dry.
After cooling for 10 minutes, cut into squares.
If you do not squeeze the zucchini well, the mücver stays doughy.
Serve lukewarm or cold with garlic yogurt.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Baked mushrooms with kashar
500 g large button mushrooms
2 tablespoons butter (melted)
80 g grated kashar
Half a teaspoon thyme
Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth, remove the stems and chop them finely.
Sauté the chopped stems with half the butter and the garlic in a pan for 4 minutes; add the parsley, salt, pepper and thyme.
Turn the mushroom caps upside down in a baking dish and brush the insides with the remaining butter.
Divide the stem filling among the caps and sprinkle with kashar.
Bake for 15–18 minutes until the mushrooms release their juices and the kashar is golden.
Do not wash the mushrooms; they absorb water and turn rubbery.
Serve hot as a starter or side dish.
Keeps 1 day in the fridge.
Zucchini gratin
4 medium zucchini (half-moons)
1.5 cups milk
2 egg yolks
100 g grated kashar
Sauté the zucchini in a little olive oil for 5 minutes so they stay firm, and drain off the excess liquid.
Toast the flour in butter for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and cook for 3 minutes until thick.
Quickly whisk the egg yolks into the sauce off the heat; add salt, pepper, dill and half the kashar.
Spread the zucchini in a baking dish, pour the sauce over and sprinkle with the remaining kashar.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until golden on top.
If you do not drain the zucchini, the gratin turns watery.
Serve hot as a side dish to the main course.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Roasted cauliflower
1 medium cauliflower (separated into florets)
1 dessert spoon sweet paprika
1 clove garlic (grated)
1 cup strained yogurt
Juice of half a lemon
Preheat the oven to 220 °C and line a tray with baking paper.
Toss the cauliflower well with olive oil, paprika, cumin and salt.
Spread on the tray without overlapping.
Roast for 25–30 minutes, turning once halfway, until the edges are deep golden.
Meanwhile mix the yogurt, garlic and lemon juice.
Place the cauliflower on the yogurt sauce and serve with chopped parsley.
High heat and a single layer make the cauliflower roast instead of steaming.
Serve lukewarm with the yogurt sauce as a meze or side dish.

Rice pudding (sütlaç)
Half a cup rice
1.5 cups water
1 litre milk
1 cup sugar
2 tablespoons rice flour
Half a cup cold milk (for the rice flour)
1 packet vanillin
1 teaspoon cinnamon
Wash the rice and cook it in the water for 15 minutes until absorbed.
Add the milk and once it boils, cook over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the sugar and cook for 5 more minutes.
Dissolve the rice flour in the cold milk and add while stirring; cook for 5 minutes until thick.
Add the vanillin, divide among bowls and sprinkle with cinnamon once cool.
Stir constantly with a wooden spoon so it does not stick to the bottom.

Milk pudding (muhallebi)
3 tablespoons rice flour
2 tablespoons wheat starch
For the top: 2 tablespoons pistachios or coconut
Whisk the milk, sugar, rice flour and starch in a pot while still cold.
Bring to the boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
After boiling, cook 5 more minutes until it coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from the heat and add the butter and vanillin.
Divide among bowls, let cool and decorate the top.
Wetting the bowls helps the pudding come out easily.
Ta-2-unique-13
Banana oat cookies
2 ripe bananas
1.5 cups oats
Half a cup raisins or chocolate chips
2 tablespoons peanut butter
1 dessert spoon cinnamon
1 pinch salt
Preheat the oven to 180 °C and line a tray with paper.
Mash the bananas with a fork and mix with the peanut butter.
Add the oats, cinnamon, salt and raisins and leave for 5 minutes.
Drop flat rounds onto the tray with a spoon.
Bake for 15 minutes until the edges brown; cool on the tray.
The cookies are soft while warm and firm up as they cool.
With tea or milk.
4 days in an airtight container.
Ta-3-unique-14
Apple crumble
5 apples
3 tablespoons brown sugar
1 cup flour
Half a cup sugar
Half a cup oats
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Peel and slice the apples; mix with lemon juice, brown sugar and cinnamon and spread in a baking dish.
Mix the flour, sugar and oats, add the cold butter and rub until sandy.
Sprinkle the crumbs evenly over the apples.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden on top.
Tart apples (Granny Smith) give a more balanced flavor.
Serve lukewarm with vanilla ice cream.

Baked pears with walnuts
4 pears
4 tablespoons walnut kernels
2 tablespoons honey
Peel the pears, cut them in half and scoop out the core.
Arrange in a baking dish and fill the hollows with walnuts.
Mix the honey, cinnamon and melted butter and drizzle over; pour water into the bottom of the dish.
Bake for 30 minutes until the pears are soft; spoon the juices over them from time to time.
Slightly underripe pears hold their shape in the oven.
Lukewarm, with clotted cream or yogurt.
